item.title: How to Give a Local LLM Memory (Ollama, SQLite, Python)
item.description: A local LLM has no memory of its own. Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp process each request and keep nothing. To give a local LLM memory, use a chat app with a memory feature (Open WebUI, AnythingLLM), connect a local MCP memory server, or build it: save facts to SQLite or a local vector store, embed them with a local model, and add the relevant ones to each prompt. For a lightweight open-source agent in Python with SQLite memory on Ollama, use Agno (Apache-2.0) or the short script below. Every tool here is free to run locally, with no usage limits beyond your hardware (licenses). To run the Claude Code coding agent on a local Ollama model, see Claude Code with Ollama.
